title: Informal Hodge counterexample attempt: explicit Weil-class audit, block 2
main_result: Constructed explicit Hodge classes and algebraic seed realizations; one representative obstructs, but replacement factorizations defeat the tested counterexample path.
corrections_to_previous_response: Unspecified generators of complex determinant lines do not themselves fix rational classes; explicit integral u,v are used here.
A Chow component carrying a nonzero primitive w as an effective cycle cannot be the desired target. Signed cycles must be included, or use P_W on arbitrary effective cycles.
A pointwise tangent rank bound at selected graph cycles does not bound all components of a cycle space.
Failure of the graph representative to deform does not imply failure of algebraicity. Alternative divisor factorizations were found.
The sign E=Im h here uses the conjugate-linear-first hermitian convention; the prior response did not specify that convention.
proof_boundary: All 924 basis tests are exact finite-dimensional exterior algebra, not a search over algebraic cycles.
All 18 tangent tests are first order. Persistence of W over the full Weil domain additionally uses the determinant Hodge-type argument.
Graph-preserving tangent dimensions 3 and 6 apply only to the chosen graph at the respective seeds.
The 5-complex-dimensional product locus uses known algebraicity for Weil fourfolds and the classical Lefschetz (1,1) theorem on the surface factor.
The explicit nilpotent has rank 4 over Q, but an algebraic semistable degeneration was not constructed from it.
No Lean build was run. No nonalgebraicity was proved. No novel theorem is claimed.
precise_remaining_question: For a fully mixed member of the discriminant -3 Weil family, does there exist an algebraic threefold Z with (integral_Z u, integral_Z v) != (0,0)? One such Z generates both Weil directions via P_W and [1+i]^*.
what_the_counterexample_would_require: A proof that both periods vanish on every algebraic threefold while u,v remain nonzero rational (3,3) classes.
